title: Parliament Ousts Two Hardline Critics of US Talks From Security Committee Leadership
detail: During internal leadership elections as parliament reconvened after a four-month suspension, Mahmoud Nabavian lost his post as first deputy chairman and Ebrahim Rezaei was replaced as spokesperson of parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee. Both had been vocal opponents of diplomacy with Washington; Nabavian called any agreement 'an absolute loss' for Iran and faced scrutiny after publicly citing what he claimed were confidential communications from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, prompting state broadcaster IRIB to suggest legal action. The removals reflect a power shift toward the camp of Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's lead negotiator, amid growing conservative divisions over talks with the US following the ceasefire's collapse.

media.caption: Iran's parliament reconvenes; hardline security committee leaders ousted

title: Treasury Expands Sanctions on Shamkhani Oil Shipping Empire
detail: OFAC imposed sanctions on more than 50 individuals, entities, and vessels tied to Hossein Shamkhani's shipping network, including operational chief Ali Rakhbarmadani, an Iranian-Russian dual national accused of coordinating shipments and encouraging Russian partners to circumvent the G7 oil price cap. The network transports Iranian and Russian oil and petroleum products to global buyers, generating tens of billions of dollars in profit, and has now had more than 200 individuals, entities, and vessels sanctioned across actions dating to July 2025. The move builds on Treasury's ongoing economic pressure campaign following Iran's renewed attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

media.caption: US Treasury expands sanctions on Iran's shadow oil shipping network
